answer: Because the plume stake is held until the terrace settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the orchard audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 14% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. A farm running 23 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. That is 39 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
